> **These notes are unfinished intentionally.** They reflect what we have actually done so far and will grow from student contributions.

## What we covered

### Course routines and Name Tag V1

We started with a simple design problem: make it easier for people in the room to know who you are.

That gave us an early example of a design requirement. A name tag has to communicate clearly before it can be decorative.

[Open the Day 1 slides](https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/13mZGVRNaV3wSsPbIsSpDiUbqsf3wodD9B2S4o3FlGfU/edit?usp=drivesdk)

### Personal identity

The next work asked a broader question: what would you want another person to understand about you?

We used the **About Me** work and **Past, Present & Becoming** to think about experiences, interests, communities, skills, and goals.

[Open the Day 2 slides](https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/179KoqehzeFEvnHdgYRZquYr3VUNWWlUdBFc1gYwmJCw/edit?usp=drivesdk)

### Listening and learning about other people

Identity is not only self-description. We also practised listening carefully while classmates presented and recording what we learned.

[Open the Day 3 slides](https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1kdgpkph9nl6B__hGIxhg0mZ9ToHrgKMQWiSujPfCHNs/edit?usp=drivesdk)

### Technical description and communication

We then shifted toward describing things clearly enough that another person could understand what we meant.

That is an important technology skill: communication is part of the design.

[Open the Day 4 slides](https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1TYn09e61daKv3hc8gKJg6Q65Du8a3mTwboVOGYrdFog/edit?usp=drivesdk)

### Funday Friday: Machine Charades

We used machine charades as a low-stakes way to communicate an idea without relying only on words.

## From personal identity to group identity

A person has an identity, but groups do too.

Groups develop shared:

- stories
- language
- symbols
- colours
- routines
- expectations

That gives us a bridge from **personal identity** to **group identity**, and eventually to visual identity and logo design.
